name: v3.24.0
body:
This release adds `vale test`, a test runner for your rules. A rule that matches nothing still loads, runs, and reports success. You only find out it's broken when it misses something. Now each rule can carry its own test cases: a short document, and the alerts linting it should produce.

    extends: existence
    message: "Consider removing '%s'."
    tokens:
      - perhaps
    tests:
      - name: flags a hedge
        input: Perhaps we should ship.
        want: |
          1:1:House.Hedging:Consider removing 'Perhaps'.

Running `vale test` lints each case and shows a diff when the output doesn't match. A case can pin the exact output (`want`), check for part of it (`contains`), or check that something is left alone (`absent`). It can run one rule on its own or go through your project's configuration, and it can read its input as another format or through a View. `script` rules are tested the same way. `--coverage` fails any rule that no case makes fire, and the exit codes are built for CI.

See [Testing](https://docs.vale.sh/topics/testing) and the [announcement post](https://vale.sh/blog/testing-rules).

## Changelog
* 2ee78171 fix: A rule whose `tests` don't parse fails `vale test` instead of vanishing
* 77da0b08 refactor: Typed errors, pattern errors at the token, and readable contexts
* 634b321c fix: Errors show the real exit code, honor --no-color, and point at the config
* db39c406 feat: `BasedOnStyles = NONE`, the spelled-out empty value
* bc8b91d8 perf: Don't parse a file no rule can run on
* c283a4dc feat: Conditional sections, `[glob if expr]`
* 08923bdf feat: `vale test`, and install a package's own dependencies for it
* 424f6e62 fix: Keep a fenced block skipped when both `pre` and `code` are in SkippedScopes
* 84deb6c3 fix: Keep non-breaking and narrow spaces beside inline markup
* 8cbda873 feat(code): parse C# comments with the C# grammar (#1196)
* 24f277bb test: add `vale test` cases
